name: ssh
description: The Secure Shell client: encrypted remote terminal access, command execution, and tunneling — the backbone of Linux server administration.

flags.description: Remote port forwarding (expose a local service).

examples.explanation: Opens an interactive shell on the remote server. First connection asks to verify the host key fingerprint.
Connects to a server whose SSH listens on port 2222 (a modest brute-force reduction).
Runs a command remotely and returns — the basis of all remote automation.
Tunnels the server's PostgreSQL (5432) to your machine's port 5433. Connect your DB client to localhost:5433 — encrypted through SSH.
Key-based connection with debug output — the standard fix for "permission denied (publickey)".

about: SSH authenticates either with passwords or, far better, with key pairs: the private key stays on your machine, the public key goes into ~/.ssh/authorized_keys on the server. Config lives in ~/.ssh/config, letting you define host aliases, users, ports, and keys: Host prod / HostName 203.0.113.10 / User deploy.
useCases: Automated remote commands in scripts and CI.
mistakes: Chasing password prompts when the real problem is key permissions — private keys must be chmod 600.
warnings: Never share or commit private keys. If a key leaks, remove its public half from all authorized_keys immediately.
distroNotes: OpenSSH is universal on Linux/macOS; Windows 10+ includes an OpenSSH client.
